title: Policy engine: deterministic bucketing evaluator for route experiments
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Implements deterministic experiment assignment (A/B/n) in the policy engine for route-level experiments. Adds a new evaluator that (1) chooses an experiment for a route (per existing precedence rules), (2) derives a stable stickiness key using defined precedence, and (3) buckets requests into variants based on configured traffic allocations. Includes safe defaults when the request does not provide an acceptable identifier, plus unit tests and a small perf harness to ensure the added routing step stays under budget. Context: This is the data-plane piece needed for Phase 1 (router integration behind flag) and follows ADR-047 deterministic bucketing strategy.

What changed: Added `ExperimentBucketingEvaluator` to the policy engine evaluation pipeline. Stickiness key precedence (highest to lowest): 1) explicit `x-redwood-sticky-key` request header, 2) authenticated `customer_id` (org/account), 3) `api_key_id`, 4) `user_id` (if present in request context from SDK-auth), otherwise treated as missing/invalid. We intentionally do NOT default to IP/user-agent because of low entropy and privacy/consistency concerns across regions.

Bucketing details: Uses a stable 64-bit hash (xxhash64 w/ fixed seed) over `{experiment_id}:{stickiness_key}` and maps to a float in [0, 1). Allocation is evaluated against normalized cumulative weights to choose `variant_id`. The evaluator emits an `assignment_reason` (explicit_key | customer_id | api_key_id | user_id | missing_key_default) to help with debugging and skew investigations.

Safe defaults: If no eligible stickiness key is available, we deterministically assign the request to the control variant (first variant by config order) and mark the assignment reason as `missing_key_default`. This prevents accidental skew from low-entropy fallbacks and makes it obvious in metrics when attribution/assignment quality is compromised.

Tests: Adds unit tests for determinism across process restarts, precedence behavior (header overrides everything), split accuracy (Monte Carlo distribution within tolerance), and missing-key handling (always control). Adds a regression test for the "low entropy" bug class (previous prototype defaulted to a constant key in some codepaths).

Perf: Adds a micro-benchmark for evaluator hot-path (hash + allocation scan) with p50/p95 reporting under CI perf job. Current numbers on CI runners: ~0.7µs p50 / ~1.4µs p95 for 2 variants, and ~1.1µs p50 / ~2.3µs p95 for 5 variants (non-blocking). This is within the budget agreed with routing owners.

Rollout: Evaluator is wired but gated behind `route_experiments_enabled` in policy context; when disabled, behavior is unchanged. Next PRs will plumb assignment into request context and add attribution dimensions to traces/metrics.
commits: policy: stickiness key resolver w/ precedence and validation
tests: determinism + split accuracy + missing key defaults
perf: add microbench for bucketing evaluator hot-path
docs: inline comments + debug reason codes
review_conversation:
Jada Williams (review): Can we clarify precedence in code comments to match ADR? Also, what happens if the header is present but empty/too short? Jordan Lee (author): Updated comments to match ADR-047 and added validation: header must be >= 8 chars and not all whitespace; otherwise treated as missing and falls through to next key.

Ethan Park (review): Any concerns about cross-region determinism if customer_id formatting changes (e.g., numeric vs UUID)? Jordan Lee (author): Resolver normalizes to string and prefixes key type (`cust:`/`key:`/`user:`/`hdr:`) before hashing, so collisions across namespaces are avoided; added a test case for numeric ids.

Mina Haddad (review): Allocation scan is O(n). Fine for <=5 variants, but can we guard max variants? Jordan Lee (author): Guardrails are enforced in control plane validation (ENG-9021). Added a defensive check in evaluator to cap at 10 variants and fail-closed to control with a warning log (should be unreachable).

Allison Grant (review): Please add a counter/gauge we can later attribute for missing_key_default rate. Jordan Lee (author): Added `assignment_reason` field to the evaluation output so the router can tag it into metrics without increasing cardinality too much; follow-up in telemetry PR.

Jada Williams (approval): Looks good after fixes; perf numbers are within budget. Approved.

Ethan Park (approval): Approved; safe-default behavior aligns with our reliability stance.
release_notes: Internal: Adds deterministic bucketing evaluator in policy engine for route experiments (gated behind flag). No customer-facing behavior change until feature flag is enabled.
